title: A Framework for Learning and Reliability Certification in Neural Polar Decoding
summary: This paper investigates a framework that connects network training, independently certified population risk and sequential reliability in neural polar decoding. Network outputs determine information-bit decisions by their signs. Posterior mean-squared error (MSE) controls bit-error rate (BER), and a first-error identity connects errors evaluated with true preceding bits to sequential block-error rate (BLER). Three methods exploit sequential decoding structure to certify changes to trained receivers. First, distances from trained outputs to the zero decision threshold, termed learned margins, yield reliability bounds for over-parameterized neural network (ONN) updates subject to separate mean-squared output-change constraints at information positions. Second, a shared loss takes the largest block-error indicator difference between candidate decoders and successive cancellation (SC) on each frame. Its expectation bounds the corresponding BLER differences, termed excess BLER, for all fixed combinations of information-position implementations. An exact expression quantifies the gap between this shared bound and the largest BLER difference among fixed decoders. Third, verified linear programming (LP) and candidate-set subdivision tighten these guarantees with controllable computation at fixed confidence. ONN experiments assess conditional fitting and weight updates. Polar factor-graph experiments demonstrate reusable combination guarantees and storage reduction under prescribed excess-BLER allowances. Component timing identifies the dominant graph-propagation cost.

title: BFLA: Block-Filtered Long-Context Attention Mechanism
summary: We propose Block-Filtered Long-Context Attention (BFLA), a training-free sparse prefill method that combines deterministic Lightning-style block indexing, query-tile sharing, and length-adaptive Ratio-$K$ selection with block-sparse execution. BFLA evaluates attention using the original Q/K/V, requires no retraining or per-model parameter retuning, and integrates with vLLM while preserving native decoding. For fixed Q/K/V, we bound local attention-output error in terms of the omitted attention mass, indexer-score distortion, retention budget, and query-tile sharing. Evaluations on Gemma4-E4B-IT, Qwen3.6-27B, Qwen3.8-27B, and Qwen3.8-Flash-Next across LongBench-v2, RULER, InfiniteBench, and Terminal Bench 2.1 show BFLA matches or even outperforms dense baselines. BFLA shows up to approximately $4\times$ time-to-first-token and $3.72\times$ end-to-end request speedups over the corresponding dense-prefill baselines. Comparisons with state-of-the-art FlashPrefill V2 and Qwen Sparse Attention also demonstrate that BFLA has better performance and efficiency trade-offs. These findings highlight the value of BFLA for the acceleration of long-context serving. Project website: https://github.com/Alicewithrabbit/BFLA.

title: A sharp analysis of Root-MUSIC: locations of correct and extraneous roots
comments: 30 pages; to appear in Sampling Theory, Signal Processing, and Data Analysis
summary: Root-MUSIC is a spectral estimation algorithm that approximates the unknown signal frequencies by constructing a high-degree polynomial and finding a subset of roots which are closest to the complex unit circle. Previous works found asymptotic expectation formulas for the performance of Root-MUSIC under the implicit assumption that the aforementioned root selection criterion does not select extraneous roots -- those which are unrelated to the correct parameters. This paper removes the need for this assumption by showing all extraneous roots lie outside an annulus of a certain thickness and therefore are not selected by the algorithm. This paper also provides sharp and non-asymptotic error bounds for the correct roots in terms of fundamental model parameters. All results hold under a natural separation condition on the correct signal frequencies and are applicable in both the single- and multi-snapshot models. Numerical simulations confirm our theory. The main mathematical insight of this paper is a geometric property of the Root-MUSIC polynomial: its correct roots are highly stable to noise while its extraneous roots must lie outside of an annulus.
comment: 30 pages; to appear in Sampling Theory, Signal Processing, and Data Analysis

title: C-MambaPose: Phase-Preserving Complex Mamba for Cross-Environment Wi-Fi Human Pose Estimation
summary: Cross-environment generalization remains a fundamental challenge for Wi-Fi-based human pose estimation (HPE), as environmental multipath can drastically alter Channel State Information (CSI) for the same human motion. Existing approaches often discard CSI phase or collapse complex signals into real-valued features early, losing motion-sensitive phase dynamics. We present C-MambaPose, a phase-preserving complex-valued state-space framework for robust cross-environment Wi-Fi 3D HPE. Our key insight is to preserve complex phase relationships throughout spatiotemporal modeling, rather than using phase only as an input feature. C-MambaPose sanitizes synchronization-induced phase errors and employs a Spatiotemporal Complex Mamba encoder with dynamic multi-scale receptive fields to capture long-range phase-amplitude dynamics. Cross-attention then maps the learned representations to human joints, followed by a skeleton-aware GraFormer decoder for anatomically coherent pose estimation. Experiments on MM-Fi show that C-MambaPose achieves strong performance across all settings, with the largest gains in unseen environments, reaching $298.5$ mm and $317.6$ mm MPJPE on the two cross-environment protocols using only $3.78$ M parameters and no pretraining. Ablations further show that prematurely discarding complex phase relationships substantially degrades performance, demonstrating their importance for cross-environment Wi-Fi HPE.

title: Radio Resource Allocation for Beam Hopping Scheduling in LEO Satellite Communications: A Spatio-Temporal Perspective
summary: Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite networks face critical challenges in radio resource allocation due to dynamic traffic demands and stringent interference constraints. Beam-hopping (BH) technology offers a promising solution by enabling dynamic beam resource allocation across spatial and temporal domains. In this paper, we propose a Tabu Search-based spatio-temporal BH resource allocation strategy for LEO satellite communication systems. Specifically, the BH scheduling problem is formulated to maximize user demand satisfaction under interference constraints. To solve this problem efficiently, the proposed Tabu Search framework integrates adaptive tabu tenure control, greedy-based initialization with interference-aware beam selection, and Simulated Annealing acceptance criteria. Extensive simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method consistently improves system throughput by 17.2\% and user satisfaction by 11.7\% compared with greedy-based BH strategies. These results indicate that the proposed approach provides a scalable and robust solution for dynamic resource allocation in interference-limited LEO satellite networks.

title: Physics-Informed Structure Anchoring With Capture-Aware Prototype Calibration for Cross-Environment RF Fingerprinting
summary: Radio frequency fingerprint identification (RFFI) exploits transmitter-specific hardware imperfections as physicallayer identity cues for Internet of Things (IoT) devices, but deep models often degrade across acquisition environments. In multi-antenna reception, antenna topology and frequencyoffset dynamics structure receiver observations, while capturedependent variation distorts target embeddings and misaligns source-trained decision boundaries. This article proposes physicsinformed structure anchoring with capture-aware prototype calibration (PISA-CAPC) to address both representation and decision mismatches. The two stages separate source representation construction from target decision correction. During source training, PISA organizes antenna tokens through a topology-guided graph, conditions propagation on CFO-derived acquisition dynamics, and applies bounded contextual residual suppression to preserve identity evidence. At deployment, unlabeled capture-aware prototype calibration (U-CAPC) estimates capture-local prototypes and recalibrates target decision scores while keeping the representation and source classifier fixed. Thus, calibration uses neither target labels nor target-domain backbone updates. On a measured WiFi benchmark with four receive antennas and ten transmitters, PISA-CAPC achieves a mean target-domain Macro-F1 of 0.9257 under a balanced transductive setting. Component ablations support complementary roles for topology-guided anchoring, CFO-conditioned modulation, reliability-aware token aggregation, contextual suppression, and capture-aware calibration. These results indicate that physically motivated representation learning can be combined with labelfree decision calibration to improve cross-environment RFFI under the evaluated protocol without changing the deployed backbone.

title: SLT 2026 REAL-TSE Challenge: Real-world Target Speaker Extraction from Conversational Recordings
summary: We introduce the REAL-TSE Challenge, an IEEE SLT 2026 satellite challenge on target speaker extraction~(TSE) from real conversational recordings. Given a multi-speaker mixture and one or more enrollment utterances from a target speaker, participating systems must recover only the target speech. Unlike simulated read-speech benchmarks, REAL-TSE evaluates Mandarin and English recordings that contain natural overlap, reverberation, noise, channel mismatch, and conversational dynamics. The challenge defines two complementary tracks: an Online track for low-latency streaming extraction and an Offline track for full-context processing. Systems are evaluated with Token Error Rate (TER), Speaker Similarity (SpkSim), DNSMOS, and target-speaker activity F1. This overview paper describes the task definition, datasets, baselines, evaluation protocol, submitted systems, condition-wise findings, and lessons for future real-world TSE benchmarks.

title: Fair Dynamic Operating Envelopes using Distributed Multi-Period Optimal Power Flow and Jain Index for Active Distribution Networks
summary: Dynamic operating envelopes (DOEs) are increasingly used to publish time-varying export limits that keep distribution networks within operational limits. Purely technical DOE allocation, however, can systematically privilege electrically favorable prosumers, while embedding fairness directly into a single-period optimal power flow (OPF) objective mixes network feasibility, equity and efficiency in a way that obscures the cost of fairness. This paper proposes a two-stage, multi-period framework that addresses both of these. Initially, a technical distributed OPF computes network-feasible export envelopes. The subsequent stage then applies a dynamic aggregate export budget and redistributes capacity through cumulative proportional fairness, limiting the additional curtailment by an admissible efficiency budget. The resulting fair DOEs are treated as first-stage decisions, while battery storage provides scenario-dependent recourse under demand and renewable uncertainty. The operational problem is solved by a calibrated regional alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) on a lossless LinDistFlow model and independently validated using AC power flow. We observe a trade-off between increases in curtailment \emph{versus} improvements on fairness, as expected, reaching Jain fairness indices close to unity. Results show that considering both storage (which alleviates curtailment impact) and multi-period fairness (which increases curtailment) is an interesting approach for modern DOE design, which in turn requires a multi-period, co-designed approach.

title: Uncertainty-Aware Parameter Estimation for Condition Monitoring of Power Converters
summary: Changes in circuit parameters can indicate component degradation in power converters, but measurement noise and limited parameter observability can make these changes difficult to detect reliably. This paper proposes an uncertainty-aware parameter estimation framework to distinguish genuine parameter changes from variations caused by estimation uncertainty. Using a differentiable switched converter model, the method requires only one or two samples per switching period. Model-derived residual whitening and a Bayesian posterior approximation quantify estimation uncertainty and reveal poorly identifiable parameters. Simulations demonstrate improved estimation accuracy over least-squares and physics-informed neural-network benchmarks, with uncertainty estimates consistent with repeated noise realizations. Experiments on a laboratory buck converter validate the estimated parameters against independently derived references and demonstrate the detection of a controlled output-capacitance reduction. The proposed framework provides a basis for reliable parameter-change detection in power converter condition monitoring.

title: SCALE-X: A Systematic Complexity-Aware Low-Precision Approach for Digital Predistortion
summary: This letter presents SCALE-X, a systematic, complexity-aware, low-precision, model-based digital predistortion (DPD) technique for power amplifiers with enhanced capabilities. The proposed approach employs a novel complexity-aware coefficient pruning method, which, when combined with optimized fixed-point modeling, enables more accurate capture of quantization effects and supports better informed decisions for implementation. Targeted configuration of model order, memory depth, and coefficient bitwidth delivers dramatic cuts in computational overhead without much sacrificing accuracy. Field-programmable gate array implementation demonstrates practical trade-offs with improved overall efficiency.

title: Low-Altitude Platform Stations for Dense Urban Connectivity
summary: This paper evaluates the downlink performance of 5G non-terrestrial networks (NTNs) realized via low-altitude platform station (LAPS)-mounted base stations, and compares it against conventional 5G terrestrial network (TN) in a realistic dense urban scenario. Using a 3GPP-compliant multi-cell hexagonal layout with 19 sites and 57 sectors, we model LAPS altitudes ranging from 100 to 1000 m and evaluate the average effective signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio and user throughput via system-level simulations. Results show that LAPS-based NTN deployments can significantly outperform terrestrial 5G in per-user throughput, provided the LAPS altitude is properly chosen to balance increased line-of-sight probability against inter-beam interference.

title: Multisource Remote Sensing and Geospatial Analysis of Vineyard Wildfire Impacts and Exposure: The 2019 Kincade Fire
comments: 18 pages, 11 figures, 4 tables. Accepted for publication in Frontiers in Sustainability (in press). Data: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22713181. Code: https://github.com/MohammadrezaNarimaniUCDavis/Kincade_Vineyard_Wildfire_Resilience
summary: Working agricultural landscapes are often treated as background to wildfire disasters, even though they are managed fuel mosaics, productive assets, and parts of regional infrastructure systems. We examine vineyard wildfire resilience during the electrically initiated 2019 Kincade Fire in Sonoma County, California, using an open, event-anchored geospatial framework spanning 4,581 vineyard fields (8,813.2 ha), wildland vegetation, surveyed structures, roads, overhead smoke, and post-fire greenness. Sentinel-2, OpenET, gridMET, soils, terrain, NOAA smoke polygons, an ignition-date OpenStreetMap network, and three-dimensional data inventories were analyzed at native decision scales. Vineyard pixels showed substantially lower descriptive dNBR than wildland pixels inside the perimeter (means 0.130 and 0.337). This contrast did not identify a universal vineyard firebreak effect: a segment-clustered boundary model gave a small negative contrast at 100 m (tau = -0.0166) but changed across bandwidths, failed slope continuity, disappeared in a 100 m donut, and produced a wrong-signed placebo. A 250 m spatial GAM reversed the unconditional pattern: after conditioning on location, terrain, and water use, vineyard fraction was positively associated with dNBR, while residual Moran's I remained 0.519. Beyond spectral impact, all mapped vineyards intersected overhead smoke on at least one day (mean 7.78 potential smoke-days per field), 34.2% of road-network nodes were dead ends, and inside-perimeter vineyards showed a larger greenness deficit through 2021 (recovery ratios 0.815 inside and 0.854 outside). Lower immediate spectral impact therefore did not imply complete resilience. The study provides a reproducible urban-rural informatics template separating descriptive contrasts, conditional associations, exposure indicators, and recovery evidence for decisions in working landscapes.

title: A Sentinel-2 benchmark dataset for deep-learning active-fire segmentation across 25 California wildfires, July 2020-August 2026
comments: 13 pages, 9 figures, 5 tables. Published in Data in Brief (Elsevier), Volume 69, Article 113357 (2026). Data: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22713948. Code: https://github.com/MohammadrezaNarimaniUCDavis/California_Sentinel2_Active_Fire_Dataset
summary: This article describes an open image dataset for developing and evaluating active-fire segmentation methods in satellite imagery. The dataset contains 2,148 image-mask pairs from 25 California wildfires, with acquisitions spanning July 2020 to August 2026. Each image is a 512x512-pixel, three-channel composite derived from Sentinel-2 Level-2A bands B12, B11 and B8A at 20 m spatial sampling. A fixed linear rendering is applied throughout the dataset. Corresponding masks distinguish background, SWIR-rule active fire and invalid observations. The masks were generated from shortwave-infrared brightness and near-infrared contrast, followed by constrained neighborhood growth. The release includes chip-level metadata and an incident-disjoint partition containing 18 training, three validation and four test fires. Among the image pairs, 841 contain active-fire labels; these labels occupy 0.0766% of all grid cells. A mask-blind analyst review covers 233 test chips and provides a separate assessment of the rule-generated labels at chip and connected-component levels. Reference training and evaluation code accompanies the data, including a ResNet-34 U-Net implementation with validation-based checkpoint and threshold selection. The archived images, masks, metadata and review annotations support research on rare-class segmentation, learning from algorithmic labels and transfer across fire incidents. The versioned dataset is deposited on Zenodo, with preparation and reuse software maintained in a public GitHub repository.

title: Rethinking electrified transportation: The case for dynamic wireless charging
summary: Long-term infrastructure investment often requires choosing between an established technology and a capital-intensive alternative that gains value as demand matures. For electric vehicle (EV) charging, this trade-off is between incumbent stationary charging technology and emerging dynamic wireless charging (DWC). DWC could fundamentally alter transportation electrification by enabling high-throughput charging in motion and reducing reliance on large onboard batteries; however, its high upfront cost makes the timing and location of deployment critical. Overcommitting to stationary charging stations (SCS) risks technological lock-in and forgoing the benefits of DWC, whereas premature DWC deployment can strand capital in underutilized corridors. Through a joint investment assessment framework coupling DWC, SCS, and supporting grid infrastructure across nearly 49,000 miles of the US Interstate freight network, we find that higher utilization and longer project lifetimes rapidly shift investment toward DWC, whose share rises sharply from 48% at a project lifetime of 30 years to 100% at 32 years. Contiguous DWC segments can share grid connections, enabling them to provide over six times the rated charging capacity of SCS while requiring 46% less investment in new distribution-grid infrastructure. We also find that a combined DWC and SCS portfolio reaches a maximum lifetime value of USD 60 billion, 63% above the case with only SCS. We further identify specific traffic demand, construction, and grid access conditions that shape where each technology becomes advantageous, yielding actionable thresholds for SCS and DWC deployment that directly inform long-term EV charging infrastructure investment and policy.

title: Wait to Learn: Timing the Gradient Return in Over-the-Air Split Learning over an Aging Single-Antenna Channel
comments: revised: theory reframed as instantiation of classical results, added line-of-sight extension
summary: In over-the-air split learning over an aging single-antenna Rayleigh channel, the mean returned gradient equals the antenna-domain gradient scaled by the temporal correlation. Uncorrected training collapses in negative-correlation lobes. Near a correlation zero, no nonzero scalar calibration improves the ratio of mean power to innovation power for an individual transmission, and, on the tested grid, using sixteen times as many pilots recovers only 7 percent of the training gap. Returning at the first correlation extremum with phase correction, 1.3 ms later at 3.5 GHz and 15 m/s, achieves 90.2 percent accuracy, compared with 91.8 percent with CSI. In the tested line-of-sight setting, the near-zero gap becomes negligible.

title: Wait or Rotate: Statistical Repair of the Backward Pass in Over-the-Air Split Learning Under Channel Aging
comments: v2: substantially revised and retitled (v1: "Coherent but Discordant: Rotate, Don't Invert, to Backpropagate Through an Aging Channel"). Adds 3GPP TDL/CDL, matched-normalization and CIFAR-10 split-learning experiments. The v1 claim that unitary correction outperforms inversion is withdrawn. 9 pages, 2 figures, 5 tables
summary: Over-the-air split learning returns the receiver's loss gradient through the reciprocal channel, so terminal motion between the forward and backward transmissions corrupts the backward pass. We repair the aged return at a fixed receive array using only second-order statistics. Two numbers taken from the forward-backward cross-covariance, the alignment reachable by the best common phase and by the best unitary correction, bound the main term of every repair. In the 3GPP tapped-delay-line channels TDL-A/B/C, where every antenna ages by the same scalar, the two numbers coincide, and at a correlation zero all tested fixed corrections stay between 58% and 62% accuracy, whereas a return delayed to the next correlation lobe reaches 98.4%. In 3GPP clustered-delay-line channels a statistical unitary correction stays within 0.02 in mean cross-entropy of ideal channel knowledge in all six tested profile and speed combinations, while common-phase correction falls to 69% for CDL-A at 3 km/h and the tested delay loses up to 10 points. In a two-cluster model spatial correction is decisive only where the common-phase alignment nearly vanishes (64% to 95%). With a ResNet-18 on CIFAR-10, only the delayed return trains at a separable correlation zero (86% against at most 16%), and at 30 km/h in a clustered-delay-line channel the unitary correction reaches 80% where the common phase reaches 60%. Given geometry, displacement and angular statistics, a port permutation chosen by linear assignment reaches 99.5-99.7% accuracy for hexagonal and square arrays in oblique motion without pilots or digital feedback during training, where nearest-position matching drops to 89%.

title: MS-Bench: A Condition-Stratified Multi-Speaker ASR Benchmark
summary: Multi-speaker automatic speech recognition (MSASR) has advanced rapidly with end-to-end speech large language models. However, existing benchmarks cover limited ranges of specific multi-speaker conditions and scenarios, making it difficult to reveal system limitations under diverse conditions and scenarios. We introduce MS-Bench\footnote{\href{https://aslp-lab.github.io/MS-Bench/}{Demo page: https://aslp-lab.github.io/MS-Bench/}}, a condition-stratified benchmark for fine-grained MSASR evaluation. MS-Bench integrates both public and internal benchmarks and characterizes each recording along five dimensions: speaker number, overlap ratio, speaker similarity, speaker turn interval, and acoustic quality. We stratify these dimensions into condition ranges and construct MS-Bench with broad coverage of conditions, scenarios, languages, and recording devices. Evaluating representative commercial, open-source, and cascaded systems, we find that overlap affects both lexical recognition and speaker attribution, while other factors exhibit more task-specific effects on recognition, attribution, or temporal prediction. These results demonstrate that aggregate metrics alone obscure important MSASR failure modes and highlight the value of condition-stratified evaluation. MS-Bench aims to reveal condition-specific limitations of current MSASR systems and guide future improvements.

title: Convex Inner Approximations for Safe AC Dispatch With Device Dynamics
summary: Safe AC dispatch requires both feasible operating points and enough ramping capability to reach the next target. This paper constructs convex inner approximations that connect nonlinear network feasibility, constrained device response, and dispatch-interval tracking. A fixed-point certificate enforces AC operating limits under bounded load uncertainty. Componentwise response envelopes convert heterogeneous device dynamics into affine conditions on measured states and power references. A command governor then combines these conditions with available ramping capability and a hard terminal-error bound. It selects an admissible target through a minimum-deviation objective and holds the corresponding reference while reserved fast regulation remains active. The resulting quadratic program optimizes controllable references and auxiliary variables. Tests on the IEEE 39- and 118-bus systems include 96 single-target executions and 64 transitions in continuous dispatch sequences at five- and fifteen-minute intervals. All 160 transitions satisfy the AC constraints, independent balancing-generator capability checks, and the prescribed regulation-adjusted terminal accuracy. Complete admission-cycle medians are 3.45 and 8.79 ms. A connected synthetic system with 3,200 buses and 1,000 generating units extends the computational assessment to 999 independent references, with a median cycle time of \LargeMedian{} s. The construction provides a tractable link between available ramping capability and safe, timely execution of AC dispatch.

title: Why the Swing Parameters Are Sloppy
comments: The draft is withdrawn so as to improve before resubmission. Regret the inconvenience
summary: Evangelou, Stanković, Kevrekidis and Transtrum compared analytic and data-driven assessments of parameter identifiability for the infinite-bus synchronous generator. Fisher information with the manifold boundary approximation method (MBAM), and output diffusion maps with geometric harmonics, report the same six identifiable parameters on the late window $t \in [3, 5]\text{ s}$, and both place the inertia $H$ and the damping $D$ among the unidentifiable ones. We explain this result from the geometry of the dynamics rather than from that of the parameter-to-data map. The rotor swing is a fast fibre that has collapsed onto a two-dimensional normally attracting invariant manifold (NAIM) of the transient fluxes before the window opens. The zeroth-order NAIM is exactly independent of $H$, $D$, $T_{d0}''$ and $T_{q0}''$, four of the five MBAM limits. We prove, under stated smoothness and rank conditions, that each of the four limits is a boundary of the model manifold at a distance equal, to first order in the parameter, to its current profiled speed. The same analysis predicts how identifiability changes with the experiment: neither a larger initial speed deviation nor a load change restores $H$ or $D$ in the late window, whereas the early window $[0, 2]\text{ s}$ makes $H$ the best-determined parameter. Evaluated in a physical metric fixed by synchrophasor accuracy limits, the late window identifies five parameters rather than six and the early window nine. The spiked-covariance structure of the linearised trajectory map explains why the principal components of whitened, sampled trajectories reproduce the prior-scaled Fisher spectrum, and regression on those components attains the Fisher-predicted recovery error in 113 of 114 parameter--scenario pairs.

title: Energy-Efficient Risk-Constrained Adaptive Semantic Communications Under Uncertain Adversarial Threats
summary: Semantic communication systems based on deep joint source-channel coding can provide task-oriented wireless transmission, but adversarial robustness may require substantial radio and receiver-side defensive-computation energy. This paper develops an energy-efficient, risk-constrained semantic communication framework under source-domain, over-the-air (OTA), and potentially composite adversarial conditions. Long-term total energy, including communication and diffusion-purification energy, is minimized subject to average semantic-loss, trajectory-level tail-risk, and end-to-end latency constraints. A recurrent primal-dual proximal policy optimization controller jointly adapts transmit power, semantic/channel bandwidth ratio, and purification complexity using causal channel observations, semantic confidence, imperfect attack-belief estimates, and recurrent history. A conditional value-at-risk (CVaR) constraint explicitly limits severe semantic failures. On CIFAR-100, at the unseen source-domain level $ε=12/255$, the proposed controller achieves approximately $61\%$ robust Top-1 accuracy with $\mathrm{CVaR}_{0.9}\approx0.36$ while using about $9\%$ less total energy than diffusion-only defense. At the unseen OTA level $Γ_A=-5$ dB, it achieves approximately $52\%$ robust Top-1 accuracy, reduces semantic tail risk by $40\%$, and consumes about $8\%$ less total energy than diffusion-only defense. These results demonstrate energy-efficient semantic defense under partially observable adversarial conditions.

title: Array Rotation in Near-Field ISAC: Communication, Detection, and Estimation Under Low-Complexity Transmit Architectures
summary: This paper studies near-field integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) with a rotatable base-station array under an exact spherical-wave propagation model. For a general transmit covariance, we derive a Cramér--Rao bound (CRB) decomposition that separates target-side geometry from transmit-covariance-dependent terms. We then specialize the framework to two representative low-complexity architectures: a single-stream superposition architecture, and a dual-waveform split architecture design. We characterize the communication-, detection-, and estimation-optimal rotations for each architecture using the exact finite-array model. In addition, we show how a second-order approximation yields compact approximate expressions for the optimal rotation angles. We also study uncertainty in the target state used for beamforming design through a correlated Gaussian perturbation model, and derive approximations of the optimal robust rotation angles for target sensing and detection. The analysis shows that the two architectures behave differently under rotation: the single-stream design can align communication and detection tasks, whereas the dual-waveform design exhibits a direct communication--detection tradeoff and can incur a larger communication loss when sensing is prioritized. Numerical results show clear gains over a fixed array orientation, especially for range estimation, and close agreement between the approximate and exact rotation choices. Detection is less affected by target-state errors than estimation in the considered cases.

title: SURE-Tagger: Structured Speech Representations for Compositional Evaluation and Targeted Data Selection
summary: Speech conveys linguistic content, speaker characteristics, temporal interactions, paralinguistic cues, and acoustic environments. While recent speech captioning models describe these dimensions in natural language, inconsistent attribute coverage and ambiguous omissions hinder systematic analysis across recordings. We introduce SURE-Tagger, a framework that constructs semi-structured speech representations with explicit attribute values, supplementary descriptions, and abstention under insufficient evidence. By integrating specialist observations through language-model reasoning, SURE-Tagger enables speech conditions to be consistently identified and jointly queried across datasets. We further introduce Tag-Bench, combining real recordings with controlled, agentically synthesized speech scenes and verified attribute annotations. On Tag-Bench, SURE-Tagger achieves the highest scores on 25 of 29 evaluated dimensions for real speech and 24 of 29 for synthetic speech, outperforming caption-based baselines across structural and descriptive attributes. Beyond annotation, we use these representations to construct cross-dataset evaluation subsets and reveal condition-specific ASR errors. Using a separate candidate pool, SURE-Tagger-guided selection reduces the overall ASR error rate of Qwen3-ASR-1.7B by 14.3% relative to the unadapted model under a one-hour fine-tuning budget, while caption-guided and random selection increase error in the same setting. These results demonstrate how structured speech representations can connect rich annotation, compositional evaluation, and targeted model improvement.

title: Explainable GeoAI for urban wildfire structure loss: vegetation and built environment in the 2025 Palisades Fire
comments: 20 pages, 13 figures, 4 tables (original preprint). Published in Frontiers in Sustainability, Volume 7, Article 1975724 (2026). Published version: https://doi.org/10.3389/frsus.2026.1975724. Data: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22061862. Code: https://github.com/MohammadrezaNarimaniUCDavis/Palisades_Urban_Wildfire_GeoAI
summary: Urban wildfire resilience depends on interactions among built form, vegetation condition, and extreme fire weather, yet city-scale risk models often overlook whether predictive skill transfers across neighborhoods. We developed a spatially validated GeoAI workflow for the January 2025 Palisades Fire, linking 12,081 CAL FIRE damage inspections to pre-fire Sentinel-2 vegetation indices, Landsat surface temperature, LANDFIRE fuels, terrain, and OpenStreetMap buildings and roads. Among 9,883 inspected residential structures, 5,566 were destroyed. Random cross-validation yielded ROC-AUC 0.92 for the integrated XGBoost model, but 1 km spatial block validation reduced performance to 0.75; logistic regression performed similarly and was better calibrated. Building count within 100 m was the strongest predictor, with destruction odds increasing 4.12-fold per standard deviation. Vegetation moisture and greenness showed opposing conditional associations: NDMI at 100-300 m was protective (OR 0.52), whereas NDVI at 30-100 m was positively associated with destruction after accounting for moisture (OR 1.74). Predictive information was concentrated at the 100-300 m neighborhood scale. A separate post-fire track mapped burn severity and vegetation recovery without leakage. The results support neighborhood-scale susceptibility screening, moisture-aware vegetation management, and spatial block validation as a minimum standard for single-event urban wildfire modeling.

title: GPU-Accelerated Quantum Annealing-Inspired UAV Path Planning for Smart Agriculture
summary: With the rapid advancement of smart agriculture, Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) have become indispensable for efficient coverage and path planning in grid-mapped agricultural fields. However, optimizing UAV flight paths in large-scale environments remains a complex Nondeterministic Polynomial-time (NP)-hard problem. Traditional path planning methods are often constrained by local optima, limited scalability, and slow convergence, which significantly restrict their effectiveness in solving large-scale problems. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a novel optimization framework utilizing a Graphics Processing Unit (GPU)-parallelized Ising solver. Our method mimics the operational principles of quantum annealing on GPU hardware, enabling rapid search for the minimum-energy state of Ising models. Unlike physical quantum devices, which are often constrained by the number of qubits, our approach leverages the Fixstars Amplify (FA) platform to perform parallel annealing on highly parallelized GPUs. This enables the simultaneous evaluation of thousands of potential path candidates and vast state transitions. By leveraging large-scale parallel processing, this framework's core strength lies in minimizing computation time even as the problem scale increases. Simulation results demonstrate that our proposed method consistently identifies superior flight paths while maintaining stable computational performance compared with the genetic algorithm and simulated annealing method.

title: On the invariance of risk-sensitive LQR gain under input randomization
comments: 6 pages, revised extended version submitted to IEEE L-CSS and ACC 2027, including Section III-F
summary: This paper shows that the optimal gain of the risk-sensitive linear quadratic regulator (LQR) problem is invariant under input randomization when the cost penalizes the realized noisy input. This may appear counterintuitive at first glance because certainty equivalence does not hold for risk-sensitive LQR and input randomization inflates the effective process noise. Nonetheless, the gain is preserved because the input noise enters not only the system dynamics but also the cost functional, and its total effect eventually vanishes. Consequently, the optimal gain and the Riccati recursion need not be recomputed, and the increment in the optimal cost can be readily evaluated in closed form. This result facilitates the use of risk-sensitive LQR in applications that employ input randomization for privacy or exploration, such as dynamic watermarking for replay attack detection.

title: VLN on the Fly: An Onboard Vision-Language Navigation Stack for Aerial Robots
summary: Running vision-language navigation fully onboard an aerial robot is hard, since grounding, planning, and control must share limited compute and a single-stage error is difficult to isolate in flight. End-to-end aerial policies fuse these stages into one network, giving up the observability and safety checks a modular stack keeps available. We propose VLN on the Fly, an onboard stack that keeps grounding, planning, and control as separate, inspectable stages. A quantized VLM grounds an instruction to a coarse image cell, depth lifts it to a 3D goal, a fast B-spline planner returns a feasible trajectory, and a pretrained reinforcement learning policy tracks it to motor commands across quadrotors. Across 15 onboard flights over three everyday referents in a controlled indoor volume, the stack reaches the target in 13 of 15 trials with 5.72 cm mean goal error and 39.3% average GPU utilization. In 6 additional cluttered-environment trials, the stack tracks collision-free trajectories under onboard perception gating.

title: A Novel Path-Tracking Algorithm for Automated Tractor-Trailer Forward and Backward Maneuvers
summary: Fully autonomous tractor-trailer systems are increasingly deployed in logistics, agriculture, and industrial environments, where precise and robust path-tracking capabilities are essential. However, the articulation between the tractor and the trailer introduces additional nonlinearities and significantly complicates lateral and longitudinal control, particularly during reversing maneuvers. This paper introduces a novel path-tracking algorithm specifically designed for articulated vehicles with a single trailer. The proposed method combines a lateral control law applied at the trailer level with a short-horizon predictive adjustment of the tractor steering angle, ensuring stable convergence toward the desired path in both forward and backward motion. The approach is geometry-based and requires no per-vehicle calibration or training. Simulation studies in a high-fidelity physics simulator show steady-state or final lateral errors of $0.02$--$0.05$~m on straight-line, circular, and reverse docking trajectories, which is of the same order of magnitude as, or lower than, the errors reported in the literature. Real-world experiments on a small-scale tractor--trailer robot, with the whole controller running on a low-cost microcontroller, further confirm the feasibility of the approach, with lateral errors below 13~mm during repeated reverse docking maneuvers despite a pose detection latency of about 200~ms.

title: RMS-AQA: A Two-Stage Spatial Audio Question Answering Benchmark for Real-World Domestic Environments
summary: Embodied assistants in domestic environments must infer what happened, where and when it occurred, and how to respond. To address this, we introduce RMS-AQA, a spatial audio question answering (SAQA) benchmark for real-world domestic environments. The benchmark features a two-stage question-answering (QA) format to comprehensively assess the ability of audio-language models (ALMs) to first ground audible sound events and subsequently perform complex spatio-temporal reasoning based on that grounding. To maximize acoustic realism, our dataset combines authentic real-world first-order Ambisonics (FOA) recordings with high-fidelity synthetic data generated using measured room impulse responses (RIRs). Furthermore, we provide a lightweight spatial plug-in that injects FOA-format data into frozen audio-language backbones. Experimental results reveal that the primary challenges stem from concurrent sources, far distance, and sim-to-real domain gap between RIR-synthesized and authentic recordings.

title: Symmetry-breaking in a discrete-choice LQG mean field game
comments: 26 pages, 4 figures. Originally submitted for review 5/18/26. v2 fixes issue with proof of lemma 4.3 related to terminal differentiability of the linearized scalar map, and other minor issues/typos
summary: Mean-field games provide a continuum framework for modeling the dynamics of large, interacting populations of non-cooperative agents. This paper studies symmetry-breaking in a finite-horizon, two-choice min-LQG mean-field game in which identical agents with linear stochastic dynamics choose one of two equally desirable terminal destinations, while trading off control effort against social pressure to conform. The model has an odd symmetry between the two destinations and therefore always admits a symmetric, dynamic Nash equilibrium in which the population splits evenly between them, producing a deadlock collective state at final time. Numerical studies have suggested that, as the penalty for social nonconformity increases, this symmetric equilibrium loses stability as a fixed point of an associated scalar, self-consistency map, and asymmetric consensus Nash equilibria emerge, where most agents select the same destination. By analyzing the linearized forward-backward PDE system through the scalar map representation, we provide a proof of this loss of stability of the symmetric equilibrium. Together with the odd symmetry of the map, this implies the existence of symmetry-broken mean-field game equilibria corresponding to consensus on either destination.

title: ECG-RSI: Recursive Self-Improvement through Targeted Electrocardiogram Waveform Evolution
summary: Electrocardiogram (ECG) models need supervision that targets evolving weaknesses and remains faithful to waveform evidence. We introduce ECG-RSI, a recursive self-improvement framework combining verified waveform synthesis with feedback-guided intervention search. Signal remeasurement verifies waveform edits; construction errors guide generator repair, while learner errors motivate interventions compared on a separate selection set. Across seven benchmarks, three rounds raise Qwen3.5-35B-A3B's mean question-answering accuracy from 34.57% to 56.04% and mean classification F1 from 24.27 to 34.03. Across the retained trajectory, the preferred supervision shifts from direct reinforcement to confusion-focused contrasts. Continued feedback correction yields diminishing external gains. These results motivate separating error diagnosis from intervention selection and checking whether gains on the feedback set transfer to independent benchmarks.

title: Commanding at the Speed of Sound: Audio-Centric Referring Expression Segmentation for Aerial Scenes
summary: Referring expression segmentation (RES) aims to localize targets at the pixel level guided by human instructions. However, current models predominantly follow a text-centric paradigm that treats discrete text as the primary interaction medium for these human instructions. This assumption is especially limiting in unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) applications, where rapid response, hands-free operation, and natural communication are often critical. In this paper, we reconstruct UAV referring expression segmentation through an audio-centric perspective. Grounded in information theory, we demonstrate that raw audio provides a higher upper bound for extracting rich semantic features than transcribed text. To achieve this, we construct an audio-driven UAV referring expression segmentation benchmark named Aerial-AudioRES by augmenting VisDrone with synthesized speech, forming "audio-text-image-mask" quadruples. Specifically, we employ an ambiguity filtering mechanism to ensure referential uniqueness, and incorporate eight distinct timbres alongside 4 realistic noises to simulate authentic environments. To drive the paradigm shift from text-centric to audio-centric, we propose the end-to-end Audio-centric Referring Expression Segmentation Network (ARES-Net). Distinct from discrete text-visual matching, our approach learns to establish a direct soft alignment between continuous acoustic manifolds and multi-scale visual representations. Comprehensive experiments show that our method obtains a peak accuracy of 64.23% in oIoU and demonstrates robust generalization on a collected real-human test set. Furthermore, it significantly reduces total interaction latency to one-third of the text-based method. Our code is available at https://github.com/LemonGauss/ARES-Net.

title: High-order $L^2$-Galerkin schemes for the decoupled potential integral equations
summary: We prove Sobolev space well-posedness of the decoupled potential integral equations. Using basic pseudo-differential techniques, discrete stability is obtained for the standard $L^2$-pairing, and we deduce spectral convergence for high-order schemes employing discontinuous basis functions, or with additional element-wise tangential continuity imposed in the vectorial part of the system. The schemes are shown to be much better conditioned than a mature commercial EFIE/CFIE solver. In many cases appearing almost independent of wavenumber, mesh density, and the order.

title: Tensor-Train Isogeometric Analysis for Large-Scale Three-Dimensional Linear Elasticity
summary: This work develops tensor-train (TT) formulations for solving large-scale three-dimensional linear elasticity problems discretized by isogeometric analysis. By exploiting the tensor-product structure of the basis functions and the low-rank structure of geometry-dependent coefficient fields, the stiffness operator, mass operator, force vector, and displacement solution are represented in TT format. Two solution strategies are investigated: a block-operator formulation, in which the coupled elasticity operator is stored as separated TT blocks, and a single-operator formulation, in which the full coupled system is stored as one monolithic TT operator. A matrix-free three-field TT conjugate-gradient solver is introduced for the block formulation, while AMEn is used for the single-operator formulation. Numerical examples demonstrate substantial compression of both operators and solutions compared with conventional sparse full-grid representations, showing that TT-based formulations provide an efficient and scalable approach for large-scale three-dimensional elasticity simulations.

title: Hankel-Koopman Finite-Horizon Energy Decomposition of Coupled Experimental Data: A Three-Phase Data-Driven Twin Forecasting Framework
summary: Finite-horizon prediction is challenging when observations are limited and a quantity of interest depends on several coupled nonlinear measurement channels. This paper develops a three-phase data-driven twin framework that integrates finite-horizon Hankel--Koopman energy decomposition, inverse-calibrated reconstruction using nonlinear autoregressive models with exogenous inputs, and forecast composition. Channel dynamics are identified and simulated in Hankel coefficient space, with candidate models assessed after reconstruction in physical measurement space. The resulting reduced-order model of the channel dynamics drives recursive prediction of the quantity of interest. Three theorems support the framework, establishing the energy decomposition and modal orthogonality; existence, uniqueness, and inverse stability of the auxiliary continuous inverse-calibration solution; and finite-horizon stability of the composed forecast for a fixed selected model under stated assumptions. A retrospective solar-power case study yields high correlations between predicted and reference trajectories across the considered forecast horizons, demonstrating reproduction of a constructed channels-dependent quantity of interest.

title: Matrix nearness problems: Do real inputs admit real solutions?
summary: Given a real square matrix $A$ and a nonempty closed target set of complex matrices $\mathcal{E}$, invariant by complex conjugation and containing real matrices, does the subset of $\mathcal{E}$ consisting of the matrices nearest to $A$ in the Frobenius distance always contain a real matrix? We give negative answers when $\mathcal{E}$ is either the set of normal matrices (solving a question posed by N. Higham) or the set of matrices whose eigenvalues lie in the closed left half-plane (solving a question posed by the first author and F. Poloni). For the latter problem, we also argue that the ratio between the real and complex distances is unbounded in every dimension $n\geq 3$, and this holds for every distance induced by a unitarily invariant norm. For both problems and $n \geq 3$, we show that a real input $A$ uniformly drawn from the unit sphere $\|A\|_F=1$ has no real minimizer over $\mathcal{E}$ with probability strictly between $0$ and $1$. Beyond these two cases, we prove for an arbitrary nonempty closed target sets $\mathcal{E}$ that, for almost every real input, either $\mathcal{E}$ contains a unique nearest matrix which is real, or every nearest matrix in $\mathcal{E}$ is nonreal.

title: Element-wise Convergence Behavior of Subspace Iteration
comments: The second version generalizes one of the conclusions in the first version. This generalization may lead to a considerable increase in the length of the paper. We had originally planned to write the generalization as a separate paper, but after submission, arXiv suggested that we add it directly to the original paper
summary: This paper studies the element-wise convergence behavior of subspace iteration. All results are established for both \(\mathbb{F}=\mathbb{R}\) and \(\mathbb{F}=\mathbb{C}\). For a diagonal matrix \(Λ=\mathrm{diag}(λ_1,\ldots,λ_n)\) with \(|λ_1|>\cdots>|λ_n|>0\), we analyze the modulus of each entry of the iterative matrix sequence generated by subspace iteration, both without and with the Rayleigh--Ritz procedure. Under mild assumptions on the initial matrix \(X\in\mathbb{F}^{n\times m}\), we first derive exact asymptotic expressions for \(|Q_k(i,j)|\) in the subspace iteration without the Rayleigh--Ritz procedure: entries with \(i\neq j\) decay as \(|λ_{\max\{i,j\}}/λ_{\min\{i,j\}}|^k\), and the deviation of \(|Q_k(j,j)|\) from \(1\) decays as \(\max\{|λ_j/λ_{j-1}|,|λ_{j+1}/λ_j|\}^{2k}\), with explicit coefficients determined by the LU factorization of \(X\). Similar conclusions could also be established for upper triangular matrices. For the Rayleigh--Ritz variant, we obtain element-wise bounds for the normalized Ritz vectors \(Z_k\). Specifically, for \(|Z_k(i,j)|\), off-diagonal entries with \(i\geq m+1\) decay as \((|λ_i|/|λ_j|)^k\), off-diagonal entries with \(i\leq m\) decay as \((|λ_{m+1}|^2/(|λ_i||λ_j|))^k\), and the deviation of \(|Z_k(j,j)|\) from \(1\) decays as \((|λ_{m+1}|/|λ_j|)^{2k}\). These results give an element-wise description of the convergence behavior of subspace iteration. After an orthogonal or unitary change of basis, the results could be further generalized.
